comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley disclose investments in hedge funds that involve liquidity restrictions. Goldman Sachs specifies that its investments are in multi-disciplinary hedge funds where underlying assets are illiquid, meaning redemption proceeds depend on the uncertain timing of asset liquidation. Morgan Stanley similarly notes that hedge fund investments are subject to initial lock-up or gate provisions that restrict withdrawals or redemptions during specific periods, highlighting a shared exposure to illiquidity and timing uncertainty in redemptions.

sentences.text: The firm also invests in hedge funds, primarily multi-disciplinary hedge funds that employ a fundamental bottom-up investment approach across various asset classes and strategies.

The firm's investments in hedge funds primarily include interests where the underlying assets are illiquid in nature, and proceeds from redemptions will not be received until the underlying assets are liquidated or distributed, the timing of which is uncertain.
Funds that pursue various investment strategies, including long-short equity, fixed income/credit, event-driven and multi-strategy.

Investments in hedge funds may be subject to initial period lock-up or gate provisions, which restrict an investor from withdrawing from the fund during a certain initial period or restrict the redemption amount on any redemption date, respectively.
